description: Rhode Island-only rules checked against the Rhode Island General Laws. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines. Rhode Island does not publish a numeric demerit-point suspension total in the sections used here.

questions.q: Where no special hazard requires a lower speed, the Rhode Island prima facie limit in a business or residence district is
questions.explanation: Section 31-14-2(a)(1) sets 25 mph in any business or residence district. Those prima facie limits may be altered under sections 31-14-4 through 31-14-8.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: In Rhode Island locations that are not a business or residence district, the daytime prima facie limit is
questions.explanation: Section 31-14-2(a)(2) sets 50 mph in other locations during the daytime. Section 31-14-2(b) defines daytime as a half hour before sunrise to a half hour after sunset.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: At night, in Rhode Island locations that are not a business or residence district, the prima facie limit is
questions.explanation: Section 31-14-2(a)(3) sets 45 mph in those other locations during the nighttime. Nighttime means any hour that is not daytime.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: The 20 mph Rhode Island school-area limit applies
options: On every street within a mile of a school, with or without signs
Within 300 feet of school entrances, daytime, with signs posted
At 15 mph whenever a school bus is stopped
Only between 7 a.m. and 9 a.m. on interstate ramps
questions.explanation: Section 31-14-2(a)(4) sets 20 mph within 300 feet of any schoolhouse grounds' entrances and exits during the daytime on days schools are open. Subdivision (a)(5) says that limit does not apply unless appropriate warning signs are posted at the boundaries of that 300-foot area.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: A person charged with driving under the influence in Rhode Island is guilty of that offense when a chemical test shows a blood alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 31-27-2(b)(1) says a person charged under subsection (a) whose blood alcohol concentration is eight one-hundredths of one percent (.08%) or more by weight, shown by a chemical analysis of blood, breath, or urine, shall be guilty of violating subsection (a). The statute also allows proof by other admissible evidence.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: For a Rhode Island driver under 18 who takes a chemical test, driving while impaired is a result of
questions.explanation: Section 31-27-2.5(d) uses a different upper figure than the 18-to-20 rule. A person under 18 who takes the test is driving while impaired if the concentration is at least .02% but less than one-tenth of one percent (.1%) by weight.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: Rhode Island's commercial-driver chapter treats a person who drives a commercial motor vehicle as under the influence when the blood alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: Section 31-10.3-31(a) says driving, operating, or exercising physical control of a commercial motor vehicle with a blood alcohol concentration of four one-hundredths of one percent (.04%) or greater is driving under the influence for that chapter. Subsection (b)(1) separately makes it illegal to drive a commercial motor vehicle with any alcohol in the system.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: Rhode Island does not publish a numeric demerit-point total for license suspension. A mandatory revocation does follow
questions.explanation: Section 31-11-6(7) requires the license to be revoked for three years upon conviction, or forfeiture of bail not vacated, on three charges of reckless driving committed within 12 months. That section does not use a demerit-point scale.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: The mandatory revocation term in Rhode Island General Laws section 31-11-6 for three reckless-driving charges within 12 months is
questions.explanation: Section 31-11-6 lists the revocation periods. Item (7) sets three years for three reckless-driving charges committed within 12 months.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: Before a limited provisional license, a Rhode Island driver under 18 must present an affidavit of
options: 20 hours of practice, none at night
180 days of practice with no hour count
questions.explanation: Section 31-10-6(b)(2)(iii) requires a person under 18 who seeks a limited provisional license to present a parent or guardian statement that the applicant obtained a minimum of 50 hours of driving experience with a supervising driver, 10 of those hours at night. The same subsection says those 50 hours may include lessons with a commercial driving school or other supervised driving. Subsection (b)(2)(i) also requires the limited instruction permit to have been held at least six months, with no conviction of a motor-vehicle moving violation or seat-belt infraction during the preceding six months, and a road test.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: During the first 12 months of a Rhode Island limited provisional license, the passenger limit is
options: No more than one passenger under 21, family excepted
No more than three passengers of any age
Passengers under 21 are allowed only after midnight
questions.explanation: Section 31-10-6(b)(2)(iv) says that during the first 12 months of a limited provisional license, no more than one passenger younger than 21 is allowed. Immediate family and household members are excepted. Subsection (b)(2)(ii)(B) allows unsupervised driving from 5:00 a.m. to 1:00 a.m., when driving to or from work, when driving to or from a volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency-medical activity if the driver is a member, and from 4:00 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. for a school-sponsored athletic activity when the school provides no transportation.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island General Laws

questions.q: In Rhode Island, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island issues a learner's permit for a car at 16 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: In Rhode Island, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: Of a Rhode Island teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: In Rhode Island, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Rhode Island, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16½ years.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: During which hours may a newly licensed teen in Rhode Island not drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island restricts provisional drivers from 1 a.m. to 5 a.m., with exceptions such as work or school.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: In Rhode Island, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17½ years.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-10-6 Graduated licensing for person under the age of eighteen (18)

questions.q: In Rhode Island, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Rhode Island, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-27-2 Driving under the influence of liquor or drugs

questions.q: In Rhode Island, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Blood Alcohol Concentration | RI Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In Rhode Island, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Rhode Island brings a suspension of 180 days.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-27-2.1 Refusal to submit to chemical test

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Rhode Island?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Rhode Island can be posted up to 65 mph for cars.

provenance.manual: Safe Driving on the Highway | RI Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Which best describes Rhode Island's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Only texting is banned for all drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
questions.explanation: Rhode Island: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-22-31 Use of hand-held personal wireless communication devices

questions.q: How is Rhode Island's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Rhode Island seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island Safety Belt / Child Restraint Law | RI Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Rhode Island?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: Rhode Island Safety Belt / Child Restraint Law | RI Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: What is Rhode Island's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Rhode Island requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.

provenance.manual: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-47-2 Definitions
